Subject: Unexpected surge on Nov 16 invoice — can we reconcile?

Diego,

We noticed a large unexpected jump on our Nov 16 invoice that lines up with the partial outage you posted about last week. Our internal billing shows roughly ~2.8M tokens billed for the day, but our traffic logs indicate ~1.2M request tokens — there's a pretty big delta. Can you confirm whether this is related to the metering incident and what steps Redwood will take to correct any overbilling?

We need an estimate of potential credits and a timeline for adjustment because we have a finance review happening Monday.

Thanks,

Hi Olivia — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the stress. Short answer: yes, the surge you see is tied to a metering regression we introduced during a runtime change on Nov 16. We're already working on a corrective plan.

What I can commit to now: 
- Immediate unblock: we will pause automated invoicing for Orion's Nov cycle until reconciliation is complete.
- Credit estimate: engineering is validating exact token diffs; we expect to propose a provisional credit by end of day Thu Nov 19.
- Final adjustment: a corrected invoice and credit will be applied before your finance review on Mon Nov 22, or we'll issue an interim statement if we need more time.

Ben Carter (cc'd) will follow up with the technical breakdown and the calculation worksheet. Marissa, Laura — I'm looping you for approvals on issuing the provisional credit and communicating the revised statement.

Apologies again for the disruption. I’ll keep you posted with concrete numbers by Thursday. If you need a quick call before then, I’m available today at 2pm PT.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge on Nov 16 invoice — reconciliation artifacts attached

Hi all — following up with the technical analysis. Summary first: during a runtime optimization deployed on Nov 16 01:12 UTC we inadvertently duplicated the token accounting step for multi-chunk responses under a rare concurrency path. That produced double-counting for ~8% of requests that hit the regression window between 01:12 and 04:40 UTC.

What we did: 
- Isolated the regression and reverted the kernel selector by 03:05 UTC; full mitigation (removal of the duplicate metering write) completed at 04:40 UTC.
- Replayed request logs to recompute true token consumption for affected customers.
- Generated an itemized adjustment sheet attached: billing_adjustment_calculation.xlsx — it includes per-route and per-day deltas.

Preliminary numbers for Orion (subject to QA):
- Billed tokens on Nov 16: 2,812,424
- Recomputed true tokens: 1,198,912
- Provisional credit: equivalent to 1,613,512 token units (~$6,452 at list rate)

Attachments: 
- incident_postmortem.pdf (incident timeline, root cause, mitigation steps) [attachment stub]
- billing_adjustment_calculation.xlsx (per-customer adjustment worksheet) [attachment stub]

Next steps: 
1) Finance (Marissa/Laura): please review the attached XLSX and confirm the credit approval workflow. I tagged the rows for Orion.
2) Diego: if Orion wants a one-off invoice statement for their finance meeting, I can produce a provisional PDF today.
3) Olivia/Evan: please confirm whether you prefer the credit applied as an invoice adjustment or a one-time account credit balance.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the sheet.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Finance Analyst, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:43:07 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge on Nov 16 invoice — reconciliation & adjustable invoicing plan

Olivia / Evan — thank you for your patience. We completed QA on the recomputed usage and have applied the following: 

- Final credit applied: $6,450.88 (matches the attached reconciliation worksheet) — this will appear as an adjusted line on your Nov invoice and as a separate credit memo in your account.
- Invoice status: we paused auto-invoicing for Orion on Nov 18 to avoid premature charge. The corrected invoice PDF and credit memo are available in your account and attached to this message (link below).
- Operational changes: we’ve implemented an additional metering validation check and added a short-term guardrail to prevent duplicate writes in the kernel selector. See incident_postmortem.pdf for details.

Action items: 
- Olivia: please confirm whether you’d like the $6,450.88 applied as a balance credit (available for future invoices) or as a negative line on the corrected Nov invoice. If no response by EOD Mon Nov 23 we will default to applying the credit to the Nov invoice as a negative line.
- Marissa/Laura: internal approval confirmed to issue the credit and notify finance. Marissa will create the credit memo in the billing system.

Links/attachments: 
- Corrected invoice & credit memo: https://app.redwood.com/invoices/OR-7543/adjustment
- Incident report: [attachment: incident_postmortem.pdf]
- Calculation sheet: [attachment: billing_adjustment_calculation.xlsx]

Again, I’m sorry this occurred — we know reliable metering is foundational and we’re treating this as a top priority. If you prefer, I can arrange a 20-minute call with Ben and our infra lead to walk through the compute logs.

Best regards,
